chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Isa ibn Bashir, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When death approached Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), he pressed me to his chest, then said: 'O my son! I bequeath to you what my father (peace be upon him) bequeathed to me when death approached him, and what he mentioned that his father bequeathed to him.'
He said: 'O my son! Beware of the injustice of one who cannot find a helper against you except for Allah.'

key_terms.أُوصِيكَ: I bequeath to you / I advise you

ai.seo_question: What is the key ethical instruction regarding oppression mentioned in the final bequest of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the continuous chain of moral bequests (waṣiyyah) within the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically linking Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn to his father, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn, and ultimately to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib. It emphasizes the concept of 'zulm al-gharib' (oppression of the stranger/weak) as a critical spiritual danger, warning that the oppressor bears the burden of judgment before Allah when no human advocate remains. This narration serves as a foundational text in Shia ethics for maintaining justice even over those who cannot retaliate, reflecting the Imams' role as guardians of divine justice.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, from Isa Bin Bashir, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said;

‘When the death presented itself to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, he pressed me<sup>asws</sup> to his<sup>asws</sup> chest, then said: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>! I<sup>asws</sup> hereby bequeath to you<sup>asws</sup> with what my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> bequeathed to me<sup>asws</sup> when the death presented itself to him<sup>asws</sup>, and with what he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned that his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> bequeathed to him<sup>asws</sup> with’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘O my<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> son<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! Beware of an injustice (which) one cannot find a helper against you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> except for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Drust ibn abu Mansur from ‘Isa ibn Bashir from abu Hamza al-Thumali from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

When Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) was about to pass away he held me to his chest and then said, ‘My son, I make my will to you as my father did to me when he was about to pass away and that which his father willed to him. ’
He said, ‘My son, beware of the kind of injustice against which the oppressed cannot find any support except Allah.’”
